author: Ash

copy.intro: Maybe you've moved out of the 30 states Dillard's covers. Or the nearest clearance center has been picked clean. Either way, you want the same mix of national brands and house labels on one floor, and these six stores do that. The department stores come first, running from mid-priced to luxury, then one off-price chain for when the clearance center is what you'll miss.

bodies.macys:
Macy's is the broadest swap for Dillard's: national brands next to its own labels, in a far bigger footprint. Its 408 locations include furniture stores, but even so there's a fair chance one is closer than your Dillard's.

If you liked shopping Dillard's Exclusive, go to Macy's own labels next. I-N-C, Style & Co. and Charter Club are a few of its private brands. And if the clearance center was your regular stop, Macy's Backstage is the off-price version. There are 300+ of them, nearly all set up as sections inside a regular Macy's.

One catch: about 150 Macy's locations are slated to close. Check that yours is staying before you switch. If you're in the Southeast, Belk has been opening new stores, including its smaller Belk Market format.
bodies.belk:
Belk is the department store to try if you live in the Southeast. It's been around since 1888, and between full-line stores and outlets it has nearly 300 locations across 16 states. National brands hang next to its own private labels.

If the Dillard's clearance center was your habit, look for a Belk Outlet. They're part of that store count, under the Belk name. Belk's newer Belk Market stores are smaller, but still carry women's, men's and kids' clothes alongside shoes, handbags and fine jewelry.

The trade-off is reach. Dillard's spans 30 states and Belk sticks to one region, so outside it, belk.com and the Belk app are your only way in. There, Macy's or Kohl's will be the nearer store.
bodies.kohls:
Kohl's covers the everyday, mid-priced side of Dillard's, and with 1,153 stores across 49 states, there's likely one near you. It sells moderately priced national brands next to its own labels, from clothes and shoes to beauty and home.

The own labels are where to start. Sonoma Goods for Life, Croft & Barrow and Apt. 9 are Kohl's proprietary brands, and they generally sell for less than the national names on the next rack. Its exclusive labels, LC Lauren Conrad and Simply Vera Vera Wang, are Kohl's-only. Beauty includes Sephora, which saves a separate trip.

It's built around moderate prices, though. If your Dillard's habit leaned toward the pricier end of its range, which runs to $350 for jeans, Neiman Marcus is the step up and Kohl's is the step sideways.
bodies.jcpenney:
JCPenney is the family department store on this list, aimed squarely at America's working families. Its own collections show the price level. The Marilyn Monroe line's High-Rise Vintage Slim Jeans ($54) sit near the bottom of Dillard's jeans range, which runs from $36 to $350.

Start with Liz Claiborne if fit is the problem. The label runs from petite to plus, and its capsule of blazers, pleated trousers and A-line skirts is sold in stores and online. National names like Levi's are there too, across more than 600 stores in the US and Puerto Rico.

It also does more than clothes. There's a salon, portrait studio and optical service under the JCPenney name too, handy if your Dillard's trip was really a whole-afternoon errand run.
bodies.neiman-marcus:
Neiman Marcus is the step up from Dillard's when you want luxury houses rather than the NYDJ and Levi's end of the floor. It's a department store founded in 1907, built around a curated edit of the world's top luxury designers, with flagship stores in places like NorthPark and Beverly Hills.

Its fall line-up shows the level, with Toteme, Saint Laurent and Proenza Schouler among the names. Dillard's priciest regular-price jeans are Johnny Was at $350, so this is a different budget altogether.

So treat it as the splurge stop and keep Kohl's or JCPenney for basics. Or try TJ Maxx, whose Runway department puts high-end labels at off-price in select stores.
bodies.tj-maxx:
TJ Maxx is the stand-in for a Dillard's clearance center, and you're far more likely to have one nearby: there are more than 1,300 of them in the US. It's an off-price chain selling brand-name family apparel, shoes, accessories and home.

The section to find is The Runway. It's a high-end designer department that only some stores have, and it's the nearest thing to a designer piece on a clearance rack. TJX, its parent company, pitches its prices at 20% to 60% below full-price stores' regular prices. It also sells online at tjmaxx.com, for when there's no store close by.

Marshalls, its sister chain under TJX, sells the same kind of family apparel, so check both. But it's all off-price. For the latest styles at full price, Macy's is the better bet.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body:
Our first question: which Dillard's are you replacing? For the full department store, Macy's is the broadest swap, and Belk is the one to try in the Southeast. If your trips were mostly everyday clothes, Kohl's has the reach and JCPenney has the petite-to-plus sizing, with a salon and optical counter on the same visit.

Going the other way? Neiman Marcus picks up where Dillard's top labels stop. And if the clearance center was the real draw, TJ Maxx is the easiest to find, with a designer section in select stores and a website for when you can't get there.

faqs.a: Items bought on dillards.com that are eligible for return can go back within 30 calendar days of purchase. Purchases made between November 1 and December 11 get a longer holiday window.
It's the nickname bargain hunters give Dillard's clearance centers. There are 28 of them among its 272 stores, selling overstock, off-season pieces and returns.
In 1938, when William Dillard opened his first store in Nashville, Arkansas. The company later moved its headquarters to Little Rock and now runs 272 stores across 30 states.
